# Adoption catalogue

> Every practice in the playbook in one place. Each chapter ends with an "Adopt this" table; this file collects them so a reader, or a reader's agent, can scan all of them without opening every chapter.

**How to read it**

- **Applies to**: `Project` is a shared codebase, `Workspace` is one developer's own machine and habits, `Team` needs agreement between people.
- **Effort**: `S` under an hour, `M` about a day, `L` several days or ongoing.
- The parts are ordered roughly from "do this first" to "do this once the basics hold". The [transition playbook](../06-field-guides/01-ai-first-transition-playbook.md) says what must be true before each step up.
- If you are an agent: do not recommend the whole list. Follow [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md).

229 practices across 25 chapters.

## Part 1: Foundations

### [How LLMs work: the mechanics you steer with](../01-foundations/01-how-llms-work.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LLM-1 | Choose model and effort at the start of a task and do not change them mid-session | Workspace | S | Before your next task, set both, then leave them until the task is done or you start a new thread |
| LLM-2 | Make the agent look up version-sensitive facts instead of recalling them | Project, Workspace | S | Add one line to your instruction file: "Check the lockfile or run the tool's help before using a library API or CLI flag" |
| LLM-3 | Restart a thread that went wrong instead of correcting it in place | Workspace | S | Next time an agent repeats a mistake twice, open a new thread and put the correction in the first message |
| LLM-4 | Back every must-hold rule with a deterministic check | Project, Team | M | Pick one rule the agent sometimes breaks and add a test, lint rule or hook that fails when it is broken |
| LLM-5 | Find the lowest effort level that passes on your own tasks | Workspace, Team | M | Take three finished tasks with tests, rerun each at two effort levels, record pass or fail, time and cost |
| LLM-6 | Assign a model tier and effort per kind of subtask | Project, Team | M | Write a three-row table (hard, routine, mechanical) with model and effort, and put it where your orchestrating agent reads it |
| LLM-7 | Track cost per finished task instead of price per token | Team | M | For one week, log tokens and cost per merged change for two model settings and compare |
| LLM-8 | Keep private code away from hosted models with a hard boundary | Project, Team | L | List the repositories or directories that must not leave your network and decide the tool or machine that handles them |

### [Context engineering: what the agent sees and how to keep it useful](../01-foundations/02-context-engineering.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CTX-1 | Start a new thread for each unrelated task instead of continuing the current one | Workspace | S | Finish your current task, then clear or open a new thread before typing the next request |
| CTX-2 | Ask the agent to list its context blocks in a fresh thread and remove what should not be there | Project, Workspace | S | Paste the "list the blocks of context" prompt from this chapter into a new thread in your main repository |
| CTX-3 | Show context usage in the status line and start a new thread before it passes about half | Workspace | S | Add the model name and context percentage to your status line |
| CTX-4 | Write a handoff file before stopping any task that will continue later | Workspace, Team | S | Copy the handoff template from this chapter into `docs/handoff/` and have the agent fill it in at the end of today's unfinished task |
| CTX-5 | Compact manually at natural breaks with an instruction on what to keep | Workspace | S | At your next break in a long thread, run the compact command with one sentence naming the decisions and constraints to preserve |
| CTX-6 | Move every rule that must persist out of chat and into a file that reloads | Project | S | Scroll your last long thread for instructions you typed more than once and add them to the instruction file or a rule file |
| CTX-7 | Trim the project instruction file to non-derivable knowledge plus pointers | Project, Team | M | Delete every line the agent could reproduce with one command and add a short list of paths to deeper documents |
| CTX-8 | Add a glossary of team and domain terms to the always-loaded context | Project, Team | M | Write ten terms your team uses with a one-line definition each and link the file from the instruction file |
| CTX-9 | After an unwanted action, ask the agent which context caused it and fix that source | Workspace, Team | M | Next time it happens, ask "what in your context made you choose that?" and edit the file it names |

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| HAR-5 | Use auto mode or the sandbox for local work and keep bypass mode for disposable environments | Workspace, Team | S | Check your default permission mode and change it if it skips all checks on your main machine |
| HAR-6 | Split settings into committed team rules and git-ignored personal overrides | Project, Team | M | Move shared rules from your local file to the project file and confirm the local file is git-ignored |

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |

| INS-1 | Cut the project instruction file to an index of about 200 lines or fewer: purpose, commands, architecture map, gotchas, vocabulary, pointers | Project | S | Delete every line the agent could get with one command, then move module-specific lines into a note for INS-4 |
| INS-2 | Keep one instruction source: `AGENTS.md` with the content and a `CLAUDE.md` that imports it | Project | S | Rename the existing file to `AGENTS.md` and create `CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md` |
| INS-3 | Move personal preferences and machine facts out of the project file into your user-level instruction file | Workspace | S | Create `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` with how you want to be notified and what the agent must leave alone on your machine |
| INS-4 | Add a `paths:`-scoped rule file for the module with the most review comments | Project, Team | S | Copy `templates/rule-example.md` to `.claude/rules/`, set the globs, and write the three rules reviewers repeat most |
| INS-5 | Add a "Why this rule exists" line naming the incident to every rule and gotcha | Team | M | Pick the five rules the agent breaks most often and add the ticket or incident behind each |
| INS-6 | Put ticket prefix, base branch and plan approver in one shared values file that the instruction file imports | Project, Team | S | Create `.claude/project-values.md` and replace hardcoded branch names in two skills with "the base branch" |
| INS-7 | Convert each instruction that must hold every time into a hook, lint rule or CI check | Project, Team | M | Grep the instruction files for "always" and "never" and pick the one whose violation costs most |
| INS-8 | Give every rule a one-line `description` and add a script that prints the rules matching a diff, so reviewers read the index before any full rule | Project | M | Add `description:` to ten rules and run the script from this chapter against your last merged branch |
| INS-9 | Run a cold-start test and a monthly audit of instruction files for stale or conflicting lines | Workspace, Team | M | Open a fresh session on a small real task and ask the agent what was confusing or hard to find |

| VER-8 | Refuse pushes without a passing local test record for the commit | Project, Team | M | Add a pre-push hook that checks an attestation file |
| VER-9 | Have the agent confirm the live commit after deploy before it reports done | Project | M | Add "ask the health endpoint which commit is live" to the ship workflow |
| VER-10 | Give agents an isolated verification environment: seeded accounts, faked paid calls, capped parallelism, one evidence folder | Project | L | Create one seeded test account per agent and a seed script |

### [PR review with agents](../04-delivery/04-pr-review-with-agents.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PRR-1 | Require zero open review threads before merge and enforce it in branch protection | Project, Team | S | Turn on "require conversation resolution before merging" for your integration branch |
| PRR-2 | Add a PR body template with fixed headings and fail the PR in CI when a heading is missing or empty | Project | S | Copy `templates/pr-body-template.md` to `.github/pull_request_template.md` and add the body-check job |
| PRR-3 | Measure PR size in effective lines with a script and give each PR a budget in its plan | Project, Team | S | Add `effective-lines.sh` with exclusions for your test, migration, generated and docs paths and run it on your last five PRs |
| PRR-4 | Have the author's agent run a self-review skill (diff, size, criteria, build, full tests) before every push | Project, Workspace | M | Copy `templates/skills/pre-push-review/SKILL.md` and fill in your base branch, build and test commands |
| PRR-5 | Block agent pushes that lack a passing test attestation for the current commit | Project | M | Add an attestation script and a harness or `pre-push` hook that checks its record and names the skill to run |
| PRR-6 | Give the review agent only the diff, the plan, the acceptance criteria and an index of matching rules, in a single pass with no subagents | Project | M | Write a script that prints one line per rule file whose path globs match the changed files |
| PRR-7 | Require every review finding to cite a rule or an acceptance criterion, and write a rule when the same uncited comment appears twice | Team | M | Add the severity and citation format to your review skill |
| PRR-8 | Answer every review thread with a commit and a test, and let only the reviewer close its own threads | Team | M | Copy `templates/skills/resolve-threads/SKILL.md` and agree the thread-closing rule |
| PRR-9 | Name one person who rules on scope and send scope questions to them before the code is written | Team | S | Write the name and your scope-question thresholds into the shared instruction file |
| PRR-10 | Let review agents run around the clock and talk only through the pull request (threads, commits, labels), and track PR metrics over time | Team | L | Start one review by an agent on a schedule and check that everything it said is visible on the PR |

### [Learning after release](../04-delivery/05-learning-after-release.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LRN-1 | Write a release record with success metric, exact measure, guardrails, reversibility and a reopen condition before release | Project, Team | S | Add those five headings to your decision record template |
| LRN-2 | Give every feature flag an owner, a linked metric and a removal condition | Project | S | Add the three fields to your flag config and fill them in for existing flags |
| LRN-3 | Before expanding a rollout, compare the metric with at least two recordings or calls and cite where in them | Team | S | Watch two session recordings for the flag you plan to expand next |
| LRN-4 | Have agents file friction at the end of each task in a fixed format | Project, Workspace | S | Add a friction issue template and one line to your ship workflow |
| LRN-5 | Record the owner's answer to a recurring kind of question as a rule that agents load | Project, Team | S | Write down the last product ruling you gave twice and link it from the instruction file |
| LRN-6 | Route each learning to one destination: issue, spec, test, decision record, instruction file or check | Project, Team | M | Add the routing table to the end-of-task step of your main workflow |
| LRN-7 | Schedule one observer per release that recomputes the record's measure, keeps a journal and has an end date | Project | M | Write the observation file for your most recent release and run it once on last week's data |
| LRN-8 | Run a daily sweep that fixes or parks open friction issues | Project | M | Schedule an agent that lists open friction issues and proposes a fix for one |
| LRN-9 | Run a restore drill from backups on a schedule, on separate infrastructure | Project, Team | L | Restore last night's backup into a non-production copy by hand and note what failed |
| LRN-10 | Run a weekly report-only pass for removable code, flags, notes and routines | Project | M | Ask an agent to list flags at 100% and cleanup issues whose "ready when" now holds |

## Part 5: Autonomy

### [Autonomous systems](../05-autonomy/01-autonomous-systems.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AUT-1 | Write the level (0 to 5) next to each agent job you run and note the one missing part that blocks the next level | Workspace, Team | S | List your recurring agent jobs in a file and assign each a level from the table above |
| AUT-2 | End long tasks on a command: agree the done check, save it as `./verify`, and have the agent run it before stopping | Project, Workspace | S | Pick one failing test, write a three-line `./verify` that runs it, and tell the agent "done means this exits 0" |
| AUT-3 | Keep task progress in a file in the repo (task, decisions, steps done, open points) and start every run by reading it | Project | S | Add a `tasks/` folder and ask the agent to write and update one task file during the next multi-step change |
| AUT-4 | Run long sessions in a named `tmux` session on an always-on host, one `tmux` server per job | Workspace | M | Start one existing long task with `tmux -L job new-session -d` and reattach to it from another terminal |
| AUT-5 | Give every unattended job a budget (rounds, time, spend) and a stop file, both enforced by the runner script | Project, Workspace | M | Add a round counter and a check for `loop/stop` to the script that starts your agent loop |
| AUT-6 | Guard every irreversible action with a code-built id recorded before the action leaves, and refuse a repeat | Project | M | Find one action your agent can send (comment, email, deploy) and add a "sent" record keyed by its inputs |
| AUT-7 | Pass secrets to agents as references with a per-secret list of allowed hosts | Project, Team | M | Replace one key in a prompt or env dump with a `{{NAME}}` placeholder that your HTTP tool fills in |
| AUT-8 | Add a watchdog timer for each always-on job and a nightly fresh restart that waits for a free run lock | Workspace | M | Write a script that checks one job's heartbeat file age and restarts the unit when it is stale |
| AUT-9 | Run the five recovery tests (duplicate event, kill mid-step, offline dependency, backlog after downtime, reboot) before raising a job to level 4 | Project, Workspace | L | Kill one running job in the middle of a step and write down what happened on restart |

### [Portable agent config](../05-autonomy/02-portable-agent-config.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CFG-1 | Write a "why" note (decision, reason, what not to change) for each deliberate oddity an agent has tried to "fix" | Project | S | Create `why/` and write the note for the last change you had to revert |
| CFG-2 | Remove every changeable value from role prompts and instruction files; read it from its source with a script at session start | Project | S | Grep your prompts for numbers, versions and ids and move one of them into a startup script |
| CFG-3 | Package each recurring agent job as a role folder: prompt, run script, allowed hosts, scripts | Project, Team | M | Move one prompt you paste regularly into `agents/roles/<name>/ROLE.md` with the five headings |
| CFG-4 | Start roles from an adapter that excludes personal instruction files, user settings and unrelated MCP servers | Project, Workspace | S | Run your role with the harness's "project settings only" switch and compare its behaviour |
| CFG-5 | Keep the role-to-model map in one file and print the model that actually ran at the end of each run | Project, Team | S | Add `models.json` and have the run script read it and echo the model |
| CFG-6 | Hand secrets to roles as placeholders, with a per-secret host allow-list that fails closed | Project, Team | M | Write `allowed-hosts.json` for one role and make the HTTP tool refuse any other host |
| CFG-7 | Give each role an expectations file and run it in an isolated copy, at least twice, before first use and after each change | Project, Team | M | Write three Given, Expect, Never entries for one role and run them by hand |
| CFG-8 | Record the role folder's content hash, the model and the starter in every run record | Project | M | Add `git rev-parse HEAD:agents/roles/<name>` to the run script's log line |
| CFG-9 | Prove portability by rebuilding the setup on a second machine from the repository alone | Workspace, Team | L | Clone to a clean machine or container and note every manual step you needed |

### [Orchestrating agent teams](../05-autonomy/03-orchestrating-agent-teams.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ORC-1 | Send every unclear request through a critic that asks a handful of questions at most, and write the owner's answers to a file before any code changes | Project, Team | S | Take your next vague request, have a read-only agent list its open questions, and save your answers in the repo |
| ORC-2 | Run each parallel job in its own git worktree and delete the worktree when the job is merged | Project, Workspace | S | Run `git worktree add ../repo-job1` and start one agent there |
| ORC-3 | Plan by files: one owner per path, shared files to a single integrator, callers listed | Project, Team | M | For your next multi-part change, write a `plan.json` with a `files` list per job and check that no path repeats |
| ORC-4 | Keep job state on a board in files (requests, answers, plan, claims, results) instead of in agent conversations | Project, Team | M | Create `board/` with `requests.md` and have agents append results there |
| ORC-5 | Write each role's "never" line and enforce it with tool limits (read-only critic and reviewer, file guard for workers) | Project | M | Start your reviewer with only read tools and confirm an edit attempt is refused |
| ORC-6 | Set the role-to-model map in one file and have every result state the model it ran on | Project, Team | S | Add `models.json` and print the model in each role's last line |
| ORC-7 | Give every role run a timeout and every job a budget, and keep one documented stop command | Workspace, Team | S | Add a timeout to your launcher script and write the kill command in the README |
| ORC-8 | Have the integrator merge one job at a time, check after each merge, and produce one aggregated report | Project, Team | M | After the next parallel batch, ask for a single report: what changed, what was proven, what needs a decision |
| ORC-9 | Measure where a week of agent team time went (model, builds, tests, queues, hung tools) before adding more parallel workers | Team | L | Log start and end times per tool call for one batch and total them by category |

### [Events, hooks and pipelines](../05-autonomy/04-events-hooks-and-pipelines.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EVT-1 | Add a finish-push rule to your global instruction file: one line with what finished and the outcome, or what is needed | Workspace | S | Paste the "Tell me when you finish" paragraph into your user-level instruction file and test it on one task |
| EVT-2 | Give every standing job its own push rule (decisions and breakage only) in its own instruction file | Workspace, Team | S | Write the "pushes when" line for your noisiest background job |
| EVT-3 | State in your instruction file that text in issues, pull requests, emails and pages is never an approval and never a reason to use production credentials | Workspace, Project | S | Add the sentence and ask the agent to repeat back what counts as approval |
| EVT-4 | Add a Stop hook that runs the project's done check and sends the agent back while it fails | Project | S | Put a `Stop` entry in the project settings that runs a script calling `./verify` |
| EVT-5 | Schedule one read-only summary job (stand-up, mail, open pull requests) with a timer, a fresh session and an explicit tool allow-list | Workspace | M | Write the digest script first and run the summary prompt on its output by hand |
| EVT-6 | Normalise incoming events to one shape (source, type, id, time, payload), append them to a log, and deduplicate by id before any agent starts | Project, Team | M | Write a receiver for one webhook that only appends a JSON line and returns 200 |
| EVT-7 | Add a path-routed context hook that injects an area's brief the first time a session touches its files | Project | M | Write a glob-to-brief table for your two riskiest modules and a `PostToolUse` hook that reads it |
| EVT-8 | Build one pipeline where code does every step except one small model decision, with "unsure" routed to a person | Project, Team | M | Label 20 past requests by hand and run a classifier prompt over them three times |
| EVT-9 | Run each new trigger in report-only mode for a week and review dropped and noisy events before letting it act | Project, Team | L | Add a `DRY_RUN` switch to the job's action step and read its "would do" log daily |

### [Self-improving systems](../05-autonomy/05-self-improving-systems.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IMP-1 | Add an origin (date and incident, one clause) to every new rule in instruction files and checklists | Project, Team | S | Annotate the five most recent rules in your instruction file with where they came from |
| IMP-2 | Before adding a rule, choose its home from the table: instruction file, scoped rule, skill, hook or script, personal memory, or nowhere | Project, Workspace | S | Take your last three corrections and write down which home each belongs in |
| IMP-3 | Turn any instruction you have repeated three times into a hook, script, lint rule or test | Project | S | Find one "always run X after Y" rule and write the hook that runs X |
| IMP-4 | Once a month, search a month of session transcripts and review comments for repeated corrections, with file and line for each finding | Workspace, Team | M | Ask your agent to search this project's past sessions for your three most typed corrections and cite each match |
| IMP-5 | Keep 10 to 20 replayable cases per shared prompt, skill or role and run each several times before and after any change | Project, Team | M | Save five real inputs with the expected outcome for your most used skill |
| IMP-6 | Keep a few held-out cases outside the repository, deny the changing agent that path, and report results as bare pass counts | Project, Team | M | Write three cases by hand in a folder outside the repo and add a deny rule for it |
| IMP-7 | Run an area's checks automatically when its agent files or guarded code change, and report loudly when the checks could not run | Project, Team | M | Add a `post-merge` git hook or a path-filtered CI job for one agent folder |
| IMP-8 | Require two conditions for a change to shared instructions: checks passed on this hash, and a person approved this hash; save the previous version first | Team | M | Add the agent and instruction paths to `CODEOWNERS` and a check that compares the approved hash with the merged one |
| IMP-9 | Choose model tiers by running the same case set across tiers and taking the cheapest that passes every run; log cost, duration and cache share per run | Project, Team | M | Run your case set on two tiers three times each and compare pass counts and cost |
| IMP-10 | Set a line budget for the always-loaded instruction file and prune it monthly and after each model upgrade by removing a rule and rerunning the cases | Project, Team | L | Count the lines today, set the budget, and delete or move the first rule that fails the four questions |

## Part 6: Field guides

### [The AI-first transition playbook](../06-field-guides/01-ai-first-transition-playbook.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TRN-1 | Record a baseline before changing anything: median PR size, time to merge, follow-up-fix rate, top three review comments | Project, Team | S | Ask your agent to compute the four numbers from the last 30 merged PRs and save them to `docs/metrics/baseline.md` |
| TRN-2 | Place the project on the ladder and agree the next single rung | Team | S | Run the [project audit prompt](../../prompts/audit-my-project.md) and bring section A to the next team meeting |
| TRN-3 | Make the clean-clone build and test a single documented command | Project | S | Clone into a temp folder, follow the README literally, and fix the first step that fails |
| TRN-4 | Name a lead who confirms plans and approves changes to shared instructions | Team | S | Write the name and the two responsibilities into the instruction file or a shared values file |
| TRN-5 | Move every "must always happen" rule from prose to a hook or CI check | Project | M | List the rules in your instruction file that contain "always" or "never" and pick the one whose breach cost the most |
| TRN-6 | Gate each step up the ladder on an observable exit check | Team | S | Copy the exit checks from this chapter into an issue per rung and close them only with evidence |
| TRN-7 | Run experiments above your rung on one person and one branch before any rollout | Team | M | Pick one volunteer and one practice from a higher rung, time-box it to two weeks, and write down what happened |
| TRN-8 | Review the setup itself on a schedule and delete what no longer earns its place | Team | L | Put a monthly 30-minute review in the calendar with one agenda item: which rule, skill or hook do we remove |

### [An always-on remote setup: a blueprint](../06-field-guides/02-always-on-remote-setup-blueprint.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RMT-1 | Add a finish-notification rule to your user-level instruction file: one push line with the outcome, skipped for quick answers | Workspace | S | Paste the rule from `templates/remote/global-instructions.md`, enable the push settings and run a short task |
| RMT-2 | Start any command that runs longer than a few minutes in a named tmux session and read it back with `capture-pane` | Workspace | S | Add the tmux commands to your instruction file |
| RMT-3 | Move production secrets from settings and env files into the OS keychain, fetch them inline, and give the agent the four usage rules | Workspace | S | Move one secret from your settings file behind a `secret get NAME` helper, and rotate it |
| RMT-4 | Give every remotely controlled session a unique name: a machine prefix, and a date for scheduled jobs | Workspace | S | Set the session-name prefix per machine |
| RMT-5 | Serve web previews from `127.0.0.1` to the mesh VPN only, and check that the public address times out | Workspace | S | Serve one dev server to the tailnet, then request that port on the public IP |
| RMT-6 | Run the weak-points checklist after every change to the setup and keep the dated results next to your setup notes | Workspace | S | Run the checklist once and write down three things you have never tested |
| RMT-7 | Split server access into break-glass, admin and worker keys, restrict two to VPN addresses, and run the checks that must fail | Workspace | M | Copy `templates/remote/ssh-config-example` and run its four checks |
| RMT-8 | Run server agents as a user without sudo and outside the `docker` group, with lingering user units and git over HTTPS through `gh` | Workspace | M | Run `id -nG agent` and `loginctl show-user agent -p Linger` on the server |
| RMT-9 | Keep the remote-control entry alive with tmux, a restart loop, a supervisor unit and a watchdog that reads the pane for a dead link | Workspace | M | Install `templates/remote/remote-control.service` and save one healthy screen for the watchdog |
| RMT-10 | Run each always-on job as a named interactive session in its own tmux server, with the narrowest permission option, a nightly restart and an explicit push rule | Workspace, Team | M | Write one job's first prompt, including when it may push |

### [Working habits and anti-patterns](../06-field-guides/03-working-habits-and-anti-patterns.md)

| ID | Practice | Applies to | Effort | First step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HAB-1 | Open every non-trivial request with a "Done when:" line: a replayable scenario or a command | Workspace | S | Write the check for your next task before you describe the task |
| HAB-2 | Add a spending rule to your instruction file: ask before any paid key, billable call or new account | Workspace, Project | S | Paste the spending rule into `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` |
| HAB-3 | Send one change per request, test it, commit, then send the next | Workspace | S | Split your next multi-part message into a numbered list and ask for item 1 |
| HAB-4 | Make the agent read the newest log, transcript or screenshot and name the cause before any fix | Workspace | S | Save the "don't change anything yet" prompt as a snippet or custom command |
| HAB-5 | Run the session-review prompt on your recent sessions and adopt one change from it | Workspace | S | Paste the prompt in your main project and verify two of its citations |
| HAB-6 | Keep a `DECISIONS.md` with date, reason, evidence and a revisit condition, appended by the agent on each approval | Project, Team | S | Create the file with the last three decisions you remember and why |
| HAB-7 | Have the agent keep a `log.md` per task: tried, confirmed, not proven, not done, still running, undo | Workspace, Project | S | Add a line to your instruction file that asks for the log |
| HAB-8 | Before approving a removal or rewrite, get a list of current behaviours and mark which must survive | Workspace, Team | S | On the next removal, ask for the list and turn two survivors into checks |
| HAB-9 | Agree which paths always get a diff read (removals, auth, data, config, CI, tests) and accept the rest by running it | Project, Team | M | List those paths in the instruction file |
| HAB-10 | Make the completion check a command the agent must pass before it may stop | Project | M | Write a `./verify` script for one recurring task |
